question.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)={x}^{4}-p{x}^{3}+2{x}^{2}+5x+7.$ 

The remainder theorem states that when $f(x)$ is divided by $(x+2),$ the remainder equals $f(-2).$ Since we're told that the remainder is $q,$ then, we must have $f(-2)=q.$

Evaluating $f(-2)$ directly gives

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-2) & =(-2)^{4}-p(-2)^{3}+2(-2)^{2}+5(-2)+7 \\  & =16+8p+8-10+7 \\  & =21+8p,\end{aligned}
$$

which means that

$$
q=21+8p.
$$

Solving for $p$ in the equation above, we find that $p=\frac{q-21}{8}.$
